展示会などで知った会社の担当者に、初めてメールで自社を紹介するときに使います。中: Use this when you email someone for the first time to introduce your company, for example a contact at a company you came across at a trade show. Chinese business emails are short and direct: the key is to say who you are, why you are writing, and what you would like the reader to do within the first few lines.
青葉精工（上海）有限公司営業部の鈴木健太と申します。: My name is Kenta Suzuki, and I work in the Sales Department of Aoba Seiko (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.
先週の展示会で貴社のブースを拝見し、突然ながらご連絡を差し上げました。: I visited your company's booth at the trade show last week, and I hope you will forgive me for writing to you unannounced.
弊社は日系企業で、主に産業用の精密センサーを製造しております。: We are a Japanese-owned company that mainly manufactures precision sensors for industrial use.
弊社の製品は小型で精度が高く、すでに多くの電子機器工場で採用されています。: Our products are compact and highly accurate, and they are already used in many electronics factories.
貴社が生産ラインを拡張されていると伺い、お役に立てればと考えております。: I understand your company is expanding its production lines, and we would be glad to be of help.
会社案内と製品カタログを添付いたしましたので、ご確認ください。: Please find attached our company profile and product catalog.
もしご興味がございましたら、お時間をいただき、直接詳しくご説明できれば幸いです。: If you are interested, I would welcome the chance to meet you in person and give you a detailed presentation.
ご返信をお待ちしております。: I look forward to hearing from you!
貴社のますますのご発展をお祈り申し上げます。: Wishing your company continued success and prosperity!
青葉精工（上海）有限公司 営業部: Sales Department, Aoba Seiko (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.
突然のご連絡失礼いたします（面識のない相手に初めて書くときの決まり文句）: Please forgive me for writing to you unannounced (set phrase used when writing to someone you have never met)
〜社〜部の〜と申します（会社・部署・名前の順で名乗る）: I am ... from the ... Department of ... (introduce yourself in the order company, department, name)
弊社は主に〜を製造／〜を手がけております: Our company mainly manufactures / is engaged in ...
貴社（書き言葉で相手の会社を指す敬称）: Your company (respectful written term for the reader's company)
直接お会いして詳しくご説明する: To give you a detailed presentation in person
ご返信をお待ちしております: I look forward to your reply
初めての相手に「一直承蒙您的关照」（いつもお世話になっております）と書くのは不自: Writing 「一直承蒙您的关照」 ("thank you, as always, for your support") to someone you have never dealt with sounds unnatural. Right after 「您好！」, give your name, then state your reason for writing in one sentence. The standard salutation for a first email is 「尊敬的」 + surname + job title; there is no need to add an honorific after the name. The formal closings are 「祝商祺！」 and 「此致　敬礼！」, and a long, elaborate sign-off is unnecessary.
初めての相手へのメールで、名乗る一文として最も自然なのは？: In a first email to someone you have never met, which sentence is the most natural way to introduce yourself?
会社名・部署・名前の順で「我是……的……」と名乗るのが基本です。「一直承蒙您的关: The basic pattern is 「我是……的……」, giving the company, department, and name in that order. 「一直承蒙您的关照」 means "thank you, as always, for your support," which does not suit someone you are contacting for the first time.
「資料を添付しましたので、ご確認ください」を中国語で言うと？: How do you say "Please find the documents attached" in Chinese?
「附件是……，请（您）查收」はビジネスメールの決まり文句です。「查收」は「確認し: 「附件是……，请（您）查收」 is a set phrase in business emails. 「查收」 means "to check and accept (something sent to you)."
正式なビジネスメールの結びとしてふさわしいのは？: Which is an appropriate closing for a formal business email?
「祝商祺！」は取引先へのメールの結びの定番です。「辛苦了」は「お疲れさまです」で: 「祝商祺！」 is the standard closing for emails to business partners. 「辛苦了」 means "thanks for your hard work" and is not used to close a first email to someone outside your company.
名刺交換やメールのあと、WeChat（微信）で友だち追加した取引先に訪問の約束を: Use this when you arrange a visit with a business contact you have added as a friend on WeChat (「微信」) after exchanging business cards or emails. In China, appointments are very often arranged on WeChat, and good etiquette is to put everything you need to say into a single message.
取引先との打ち合わせが終わった当日に、決まったことを整理して相手に確認してもらう: This is an email you send on the day of a meeting with a business partner, summarizing what was agreed and asking them to confirm it. In China, verbal agreements often turn out to be understood differently later, so it is safer to have them in writing.
相手の要望を受けて見積書を送るときのメールです。価格そのものは添付の見積書に書き: This email is for sending a quotation in response to a customer's request. The prices themselves go in the attached quotation; the body of the email summarizes the terms of the deal, such as tax, shipping, delivery time, payment terms, and validity period.
支払期限を過ぎても入金が確認できないときに、取引先へ送る最初の催促メールです。1: This is the first reminder email you send to a business partner when payment has not been received after the due date. The first reminder should simply state the fact that the payment has not been confirmed and politely ask whether there is any issue on their side.
値下げ要請を丁寧に断る: Politely Declining a Request for a Price Reduction
取引先からさらなる値下げを求められたが、応じられないときに使います。中国の取引で: Use this when a business partner asks for a further price cut that you cannot accept. In Chinese business dealings, a vague answer only drags out the negotiation, so the basic approach is to state your conclusion clearly and then give your reasons and an alternative.
自社の都合で納品が遅れることがわかったとき、できるだけ早く取引先に知らせるメール: This email informs a business partner, as early as possible, that delivery will be delayed for reasons on your side. Rather than only apologizing, it is important to give the cause, the new delivery date, alternatives, and the measures you will take to prevent it from happening again, all at once.
取引先から製品の不良について連絡を受けたあと、調査結果と対応策を伝えるメールです: This email reports your investigation results and countermeasures after a business partner has informed you of defective products. Chinese business partners put great weight on whether you acted right away and what exactly you will do, so trust depends on how quickly you respond and how clearly you spell out your actions.
春節前のWeChat挨拶: A WeChat Greeting Before Chinese New Year
春節（旧正月）の休みに入る数日前に、お世話になった取引先へWeChatで送る挨拶: This is a greeting you send on WeChat to the business partners you have worked with, a few days before the Spring Festival (Chinese New Year) holiday begins. If you include three things - thanks for the past year, how to reach you during the holiday, and New Year wishes - your message will come across as sincere even if it is short.
社内グループへのお知らせ: Announcements to an Internal Group Chat
部署のWeChatグループ（工作群）で、メンバー全員に連絡事項を伝えるときに使い: Use this to pass on information to all members of your department's WeChat group (「工作群」). In Chinese workplaces, much internal communication happens in group chats, and it is common to list the key points and ask for confirmation with 「收到请回复」 ("reply when you receive this").
取引終了にあたってのお礼: Thanking a Partner at the End of a Business Relationship
契約満了などで取引が終わる相手に、これまでの協力への感謝を伝えるメールです。終了: This email thanks a partner for their cooperation when a business relationship ends, for example because a contract has expired. Explaining the reason briefly and mentioning one specific episode you are grateful for conveys sincerity rather than formality, and it keeps the door open for future business.
後任紹介と異動のご挨拶: Introducing Your Successor and Saying Goodbye
異動や帰任が決まったとき、担当していた取引先に後任者を紹介し、別れの挨拶をするメ: This email is for when you are being transferred or returning to your home office: you introduce your successor to the clients you have handled and say goodbye. Copying your successor (「抄送」, CC) and stating that the handover of ongoing projects is complete will reassure the client.
取引先に新製品を説明するため、オンライン会議を申し込むメールです。目的・所要時間: This email asks a business partner for an online meeting so that you can present a new product. If your first email already includes the purpose, the expected length, and some possible times, it is easier for the other side to coordinate internally.
WeChatで打ち合わせの日程変更をお願いする: Asking to Reschedule a Meeting on WeChat
約束していた打ち合わせに急な事情で出られなくなり、WeChatで日程の変更をお願: Use this when something urgent comes up and you can no longer attend a scheduled meeting, so you ask on WeChat to reschedule. Since you are the one asking for the change, send your apology, the reason, and new possible dates all together, and let the other person choose.
新しい仕入先に見積りを依頼するメールです。品名・仕様・数量・納期・回答期限を具体: This email asks a new supplier for a quotation. The more specifically you state the item, specifications, quantity, delivery time, and reply deadline, the faster you will get an accurate quotation.
仕入先から届いた見積りが予算を上回っているとき、買い手として値下げを打診するメー: This email is for buyers who want to propose a lower price when a supplier's quotation exceeds their budget. Acknowledging the quality of the supplier's product, then giving your reasons (budget, market prices from other suppliers) and a specific target price, moves the negotiation forward.
取引先から注文書を受け取ったとき、受注のお礼とともに注文内容を確認するメールです: This email thanks a customer for a purchase order and confirms its details. Restating the model number, quantity, unit price, delivery date, and delivery location helps prevent misunderstandings.
製品カタログを見て興味を持った仕入先に、サンプルの提供をお願いするメールです。ど: This email asks a supplier whose catalog interested you to provide samples. If you state clearly which models you want, how many, by when, and where to send them, the supplier can arrange it right away.
取引先から届いた契約書案を社内の法務部門で確認した結果、修正したい条項があるとき: This email is for when your legal department has reviewed a draft contract from a business partner and there are clauses you want to change. Showing exactly which clauses you want to amend and how, with your reasons, makes it easier for the other side to consider the changes internally.
遠方の取引先が工場見学に来るとき、日程と空港への出迎えについて事前に知らせるメー: This email tells a business partner coming from far away to tour your factory about the itinerary and airport pickup in advance. Spelling out the flight, the meeting point, and how to reach you means they will not get lost on the day.
空港出迎え当日のWeChat: WeChat Messages on Airport Pickup Day
空港まで取引先を迎えに行った当日、到着する相手にWeChatで待ち合わせ場所を知: Use this on the day you go to the airport to meet a business partner, to tell them on WeChat where to meet you. A short message with the terminal, exit number, how to spot you, and details of the car lets them check it as soon as they get off the plane.
取引先を訪問した翌日までに送るお礼のメールです。面会へのお礼に加え、話し合った内: This is a thank-you email to send by the day after visiting a business partner. As well as thanking them for meeting you, mentioning what you discussed and the next steps turns it into more than a courtesy and leads to the next round of business.
春節（旧正月）の休業期間を取引先に知らせる正式な通知メールです。休業期間・休暇前: This is a formal notice informing business partners of your company's Spring Festival (Chinese New Year) closure. Always include the closure dates, the last shipping date before the holiday, and how to reach you during the break, and send it early so that partners can plan their orders and deliveries.
年末のお礼と新年のご挨拶: Year-End Thanks and New Year Greetings
年末（元旦の前）に、一年間お世話になった取引先へ送る改まった挨拶メールです。一年: This is a formal greeting sent at the end of the year (before New Year's Day) to business partners you have worked with over the year. It looks back on the year, mentions specific achievements, and offers your plans and good wishes for the coming year. In China the Spring Festival matters more than January 1, but in business it is increasingly common to send greetings at the end of the calendar year to mark its close.
請求書（発票）の送付と支払いのご案内: Sending an Invoice and Payment Details
納品が完了したあと、取引先に請求書（発票）を送り、支払期日と振込先を案内するメー: This email sends the invoice (「发票」) to a customer after delivery is complete and gives the payment due date and bank account. In China, a finance department usually cannot start processing payment until it has received the 「发票」, so it is important to state clearly the type of invoice, the amount, and how it was sent.
仕入先から届いた商品に数量不足や破損があったとき、買い手として問題を伝え、対応を: This email is for buyers who receive goods from a supplier that are short or damaged, to report the problem and ask for action. If you stay calm and lay out, in order, the facts (quantities, photos), the impact, and the action and deadline you require, the supplier will respond quickly.
取引先に同僚を紹介する: Introducing a Colleague to a Client
取引先から専門的な相談を受けたとき、社内の適任者を紹介してつなぐメールです。紹介: This email connects a client who has asked a specialist question with the right person in your company. Describing the colleague's background and strengths, and explaining how to contact them from now on, lets the client start dealing with them with confidence.
応募者に書類選考の通過を伝え、面接の日時・場所・持ち物を案内するメールです。応募: This email tells a job applicant that they have passed the application screening and gives the date, place, and what to bring for the interview. Put all the necessary information in one email so the applicant is not left guessing, and give a deadline for confirming attendance.
担当している案件の進み具合を上司にメールで報告し、判断を仰ぐときに使います。結論: Use this to report to your manager by email on the progress of a deal you are handling and ask for a decision. Putting the conclusion first, then the current status, the problem, your recommendation, and what you need your manager to decide, lets even a busy manager make a decision quickly.
グループチャットで年会を告知する: Announcing the Annual Party in a WeChat Group
会社の年会（春節前に開く全社パーティー）について、社内のWeChatグループで告: Use this to announce the company's annual party (「年会」, a company-wide event held before the Spring Festival) in an internal WeChat group. List the date, venue, deadlines, and so on, and pin the message with the group's announcement (「公告」) function so that anyone who wants to check later can find it easily.
WeChatで取引先に手短に返信する: Replying Quickly to a Client on WeChat
取引先からWeChatで資料や依頼が届いたとき、まず受け取ったことと対応の見通し: This is a short reply to a client who has sent you documents or a request on WeChat, first confirming that you have received it and saying when you will deal with it. Even if you cannot answer right away, telling them when you will get back to them reassures them.
WeChatで上司に休みを申し出る: Asking Your Manager for Sick Leave on WeChat
体調不良などで急に休まなければならないとき、朝のうちにWeChatで上司に連絡す: This is a message to send your manager on WeChat first thing in the morning when you suddenly need to take the day off, for example because you are ill. Giving the reason, how long you will be off, and who is covering your work all at once makes it easier for your manager to rearrange things.
新しい業者から受けた営業提案を、検討の結果お断りするときのメールです。提案への感: This email declines a sales proposal from a new vendor after you have considered it. Thank them for the proposal, state your decision clearly, explain your reasons briefly in a way that does not criticize them, and close by leaving the door open for the future.
WeChatで展示会のブースに招待する: Inviting a Client to Your Trade Show Booth on WeChat
自社が出展する展示会に、取引先をWeChatで招待するときのメッセージです。会期: This is a WeChat message inviting a client to a trade show where your company is exhibiting. Including not just the dates, venue, and booth number but also the highlights and how to get in makes it easier for them to come.
展示会後のフォローアップメール: Following Up After a Trade Show
展示会で自社のブースに立ち寄り、名刺を交換した相手に、数日後に送るお礼とフォロー: This is a thank-you and follow-up email sent a few days after a trade show to someone who stopped by your booth and exchanged business cards with you. The key points are to mention what you talked about at the show, send the materials you promised, and propose a next step, such as a visit or a demonstration.
外貨建ての見積りと為替条項: A Foreign-Currency Quotation with an Exchange-Rate Clause
日本本社から中国の輸入業者に、米ドル建てで見積りを出すときのメールです。価格を示: This email is sent by a head office in Japan to a Chinese importer when quoting a price in US dollars. Stating clearly the currency of the price and of payment, who bears costs such as import duties, and what happens if the exchange rate moves sharply helps prevent trouble later.
新規の取引先から長い支払サイトを求められたが、そのままでは受けられないときに、売: This email is sent by a seller when a new customer asks for long payment terms that cannot be accepted as they are, and proposes alternative terms instead. Basing your position on company rules and offering a step-by-step plan that eases the terms as a payment track record builds up makes it easier to reach agreement.
生産が終わった製品について、出荷前の検査結果を取引先に報告し、出荷の了承を得るメ: This email reports the results of a pre-shipment inspection to a customer once production is finished, and asks for approval to ship. Stating clearly the quantity inspected, the items checked, the results, and how any defects found were dealt with lets the customer approve the shipment with confidence.
取引先が型番を間違えて注文した製品について、交換に応じる旨と手順を伝えるメールで: This email tells a customer who ordered the wrong model that you will exchange the products, and explains the procedure. Giving your decision first and making the procedure and the split of costs clear means the matter can be settled in a single exchange of emails.
輸入した貨物が税関検査のために足止めされ、納品が遅れることを取引先に知らせるメー: This email tells a customer that imported goods are being held for a customs inspection and that delivery will be late. Even when the delay is not your fault, giving the cause, the expected new delivery date, and how you will keep them updated all at once makes it easier for the customer to adjust their plans.
発票の誤りのお詫び: Apologizing for an Error on an Invoice
取引先の経理担当者から、発行した発票（請求書を兼ねる税務上の領収書）の金額の誤り: This is an apology email sent when a customer's accounts staff point out an error in the amount on a fapiao you issued (an official tax invoice that also serves as the bill). It sets out the error and its cause, how the original fapiao will be handled, when a new one will be issued, and how the mistake will be prevented in future, all at once.
元上司に推薦状をお願いする: Asking a Former Manager for a Reference Letter
以前の職場の上司に、大学院（MBA）出願のための推薦状をお願いするメールです。久: This email asks a manager from a previous job to write a reference letter for a graduate school (MBA) application. Since it has been a while since you were last in touch, bring them up to date politely, make the conditions such as the deadline clear, and leave room for them to say no easily.
グループチャットで新しい同僚を紹介する: Welcoming a New Colleague in a WeChat Group
新しい同僚が入社した日に、部署のWeChatグループで紹介するメッセージです。経: This message introduces a new colleague in the department's WeChat group on their first day. It includes information that gives everyone something to talk to them about, such as their background, their role, and where they sit, and ends by inviting the newcomer to say hello.
部署の定例会議のあとに、決まったことを議事録にまとめてメンバー全員に送るメールで: This email sends the minutes of a regular department meeting to all members afterward. Stating for each agenda item what is to be done, by whom, and by when, in a single line, makes clear what everyone needs to do after the meeting.
WeChatで提出期限の延長をお願いする: Asking for a Deadline Extension on WeChat
取引先に約束していた資料の提出が間に合わなくなったとき、WeChatで期限の延長: This message asks a client on WeChat for more time when you can no longer submit promised documents by the deadline. Put the reason, the new date you are asking for, and what you can offer in the meantime into a single message.
仕入先から届いた契約更新の案内に対し、更新に同意する旨と、追加したい条件を伝える: This email replies to a supplier's contract renewal notice, agreeing to renew and setting out the conditions you would like to add. Give your decision (to renew, and for how long) first, make clear whether the price and main terms stay as they are, and then list the additional points with numbers.
会食へのご招待: Inviting a Client to a Business Dinner
お世話になった取引先の社長と社員を、感謝の気持ちを込めて夕食に招待するメールです: This email invites the head of a client company and their staff to dinner as a token of thanks. It gives the purpose, date and time, venue, and who will attend from your side, and asks by a set date how many will attend and whether there are any dietary restrictions.
会食後のWeChatでのお礼: Thanking a Host on WeChat After a Dinner
出張先で取引先に夕食をごちそうになったあと、その日の夜にWeChatで送るお礼の: This is a thank-you message sent on WeChat the same evening after a client has treated you to dinner during a business trip. It mentions a dish or conversation that stood out, and also states the next step on the work topics that came up over dinner.
入院した取引先へのお見舞い: Sending Get-Well Wishes to a Client in Hospital
取引先の担当者が入院して手術を受けたと聞いたときに、WeChatで送るお見舞いの: This is a get-well message sent on WeChat when you hear that your contact at a client company has been hospitalized for an operation. Avoid asking about their condition in detail, reassure them that they need not worry about work, and spare them the effort of replying.
上司への退職の申し出: Submitting a Resignation to Your Manager
退職を決めた社員が、上司に正式に退職を申し出るメールです。退職の時期と理由を簡潔: This email is sent by an employee who has decided to leave, formally notifying their manager of their resignation. Stating the leaving date and the reason briefly, and showing gratitude for your time at the company along with a concrete handover plan, helps you leave on good terms.
最終出社日のお別れの挨拶: Saying Goodbye to Colleagues on Your Last Day
退職する社員が、最終出社日に部署のWeChatグループで同僚に送る別れの挨拶です: This is a farewell message that an employee who is leaving posts in the department's WeChat group on their last day. Including four things, namely thanks, memories, who has taken over your work, and how to stay in touch, makes even a short message heartfelt.
顧客満足度調査へのご協力のお願い: Requesting Participation in a Customer Satisfaction Survey
取引先に、年に一度の顧客満足度アンケートへの回答をお願いするメールです。目的・所: This email asks customers to complete an annual customer satisfaction survey. Stating the purpose, the time required, the deadline, and how the answers will be used makes people more willing to take part.
取引先全体に、新製品の発売を知らせる正式な案内メールです。最初に「何を・いつ発売: This is a formal email announcing a new product launch to all customers. It first says what is being launched and when, presents the features concretely with figures, and adds actions the reader can take next, such as attending a launch event or requesting a sample.
技術的な問い合わせへの回答: Replying to a Technical Support Request
取引先の技術者から製品の不具合について問い合わせを受け、技術サポート担当者が原因: In this email, a technical support engineer replies to a customer's engineer who has reported a problem with a product, giving a likely cause and the steps to fix it. Setting out the cause, the steps, and what to do next if the problem persists, in that order, lets the customer carry out the work without confusion.
モーメンツで会社の移転を告知する: Announcing an Office Move on WeChat Moments
WeChatの「朋友圈」（モーメンツ）に、会社のオフィス移転を知らせる投稿です。: This is a post on WeChat Moments (「朋友圈」) announcing that the company's office has moved. Since clients can see it too, write in a friendly tone while giving the necessary information accurately, such as the new address, the start date, and which contact details stay the same.
仕事のグループチャットで紅包を送る: Sending a Red Envelope in a Work Group Chat
試用期間を終えて本採用になった社員が、お礼の気持ちを込めて部署のWeChatグル: This is the message an employee who has just been confirmed as permanent staff after their probation period posts when sending a red envelope (a small gift of money) to the department's WeChat group as a thank-you. It is usual to express thanks and add a modest remark that the amount is small.
原材料や物流のコスト上昇により、取引先に値上げを通知するメールです。これまでの取: This is an email notifying a customer of a price increase caused by rising raw material and logistics costs.
